title: Armament Systems Maintenance Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-913A. Military Occupational Specialty 913A-- Armament Systems Maintenance Warrant
Officer (Effective 202010)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. AR 135-100, DA Pam 601-6, and DA Pam 611-21.
   c. MOS 913A. MOS 913A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are: 91A, 91F,
91M, 91P and 91X or 91Z with feeder MOS experience.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASIs associated with all
warrant officer MOS)).
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Complete the Warrant Officer Armament Systems Maintenance Basic Course.
              (b) Have correctable vision, normal color discrimination, normal hearing, and full use
of upper and lower extremities per AR 40-501.                         .
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Armament Systems Maintenance Advanced Course.
        (3) CW4 must-
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
   (4) CW5 see MOS 915E.
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Manages activities and personnel engaged in field level maintenance and repair of
small arms, field artillery and armament systems.
              (b) Directs procedures for the identification and troubleshooting of malfunctions in
electrical, hydraulic, fire control, and instrument items.
              (c) Establishes evacuation and replacement procedures of such items that are
unserviceable and beyond the repair capabilities of forward support companies.
              (d) Manages quality assurance and production control programs to ensure established
work standards are met and repairs are made on a timely basis.
              (e) Administers The Army Maintenance Management System (TAMMS) and other
maintenance reporting and management systems
              (f) Administers regulations and procedures pertaining to physical security,
accountability, and shipment of weapons.
              (g) Directs repair teams in support of field units and activities.
              (h) Establishes and directs a shop safety program per applicable regulations.
              (i) Establishes a technical library and examines, interprets, and disseminates technical
material, including orders and bulletins.
        (2) CW3--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Manages maintenance activities and personnel at field level.
              (c) Directs the repairs of complex malfunctions occurring in tank turret electrical,
hydraulic, fire control and instrument systems.
        (3) CW4--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
              (b) Serves as the senior armament systems maintenance technical advisor in echelons
above brigade levels of command.
              (c) Assists echelons above brigade staff in the planning, coordination, and execution of
maintenance support.
               (d) Provides technical expertise in maintenance doctrine on the battlefield for brigade
and subordinate element level commanders and staff to efficiently employ armament systems
maintenance personnel and equipment in support of the commanders’ mission.
              (e) Manages materiel readiness reporting for echelons above brigade organizations.
              (f) Performs materiel readiness management duties at sustainment command levels.
              (g) Performs research, development, test and evaluation duties.
              (h) Assists in coordination and evaluates maintenance performed by contract support.
              (i) Serves as Ordnance technical subject matter expert in training, capability, and
materiel development positions.
              (j) Advises commanders on the progression and utilization of subordinate Ordnance
warrant officers.
         (4) CW5--see MOS 915E.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold). Must achieve a minimum OPAT
score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength
Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles.
         (2) Table 8-913A-1. Physical requirements.
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-913A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-913A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

(i) Serves as Ordnance technical subject matter expert in training, capability, and materiel development positions.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
